items.note: This から means "because, so" — a different job from the から you already know for "from" (Lesson 3's なんじからなんじまで, Lesson 6's アメリカからきました). It attaches to the end of the reason clause: clause1から、clause2, as in いいてんきですから、こうえんでひるごはんをたべませんか, "The weather is nice, so shall we have lunch in the park?"

items.note: ゆき (snow) + まつり (festival, as in おまつり from Key Sentence 1) = ゆきまつり (snow festival).
Combines with ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) to form にしぐち, 'west exit'.
にし (west) + ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) = にしぐち (west exit).
Combines with ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) to form ひがしぐち, 'east exit'.
ひがし (east) + ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) = ひがしぐち (east exit).
Combines with ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) to form きたぐち, 'north exit'.
きた (north) + ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) = きたぐち (north exit).
Combines with ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) to form みなみぐち, 'south exit'.
みなみ (south) + ぐち (opening/exit, from でぐち) = みなみぐち (south exit).
すきました here comes from すきます, "become empty/hungry" — a different word from すき, "like, favorite" (Lesson 15), despite the similar sound. おなかがすきました literally means "my stomach has become empty."

items.note: なにか (something) is used in questions and positive statements, e.g. なにかのみませんか; contrast なにも (Lesson 8), which only ever pairs with a negative verb to mean "nothing."
A more neutral, slightly formal synonym of ちょっと (Lesson 10) — both mean "a bit, a little," but ちょっと is the everyday casual choice.
Verb form of やすみ (Lesson 3, "break, day off") — やすみます is the action "to rest," while やすみ names the break itself.

items.note: Contrasts with ええ、ぜひ or いいですね。ぜひ — ありがとうございます。ぜひ is used specifically when accepting an invitation to the speaker's home, a planned event, or something already decided.
